quorum.kill_rule: three lanes disagreed about whether the probe change was a regression; settling that disagreement rather than counting lanes is what located a defect older than this ticket
quorum.rounds: three sandboxed plan lanes on d14ffaaf...832cde42, base pinned by SHA: 3 FAIL, partial=false. Four claims confirmed by all three, two refuted, one of the refutations found three separate ways.
refuted_claims: The rule named three files, so a fourth controller-side read added anywhere else would have stayed green — vacuous against exactly what it exists to prevent. It sweeps all of src/ now with one file exempt by name; measured, the same call added to src/core/state/reconstruct.rs is reported by name.

The rule read its own explanation twice over: comment stripping covered whole lines only, leaving a trailing comment and a block comment as doors, and the ordering check compared string positions, which a binding above the early returns would satisfy while changing what the code does. All three comment forms are stripped now and each predicate must sit in a guard whose body RETURNS. Third instance of this shape in the repository, after RULE 8 and the cargo PATH prelude.

Two lanes called the probe change a regression: a missing probe means the planner skips the staleness check, so a namespaced task stops rebuilding when its sources change. The third lane answered that the old behaviour did not detect those changes either, since it hashed the controller — and was right. The planner cannot tell 'probed, nothing stale' from 'never probed', which has been true for EVERY non-local machine since the probe existed. Filed as forjar#497. This ticket's trade, a silent gap in place of a confident wrong answer about the wrong filesystem, is deliberate and named.

crux.verdict: all three make the mistake unrepresentable by putting the boundary in the API rather than in a predicate: a container or machine is named, and there is no call that accidentally reads the host path instead. forjar's boundary is a function each caller must remember to consult, which is why this defect appeared at four call sites and needed a tree-wide rule to keep it away. accept(the transport design, which buys one place to run from) and reject(the predicate-per-caller shape). Two tickets have now fixed instances; the rule added here is a guard rather than a cure.
